hints: Take natural logarithms and use the power, product, and quotient laws on 2^(3x−4)=3/5^x.
Collect the x-terms, solve exactly, and combine each group of logarithms into the logarithm of a single integer to match the required ln m/ln n form.
walkthrough:
Take the natural logarithm of both sides of $2^{3x-4} = \dfrac{3}{5^x}$:
$$\ln\left(2^{3x-4}\right) = \ln\left(\dfrac{3}{5^x}\right)$$

Apply the quotient and power laws of logarithms $\ln(u/v) = \ln u - \ln v$ and $\ln\left(u^k\right) = k\ln u$:
$$(3x - 4)\ln 2 = \ln 3 - \ln\left(5^x\right)$$
$$3x\ln 2 - 4\ln 2 = \ln 3 - x\ln 5$$

Collect terms involving $x$ on the left-hand side and constants on the right-hand side:
$$3x\ln 2 + x\ln 5 = \ln 3 + 4\ln 2$$
$$x(3\ln 2 + \ln 5) = \ln 3 + 4\ln 2$$

Express the coefficients as single logarithms using power and product laws:
$$\text{Numerator: } \ln 3 + 4\ln 2 = \ln 3 + \ln\left(2^4\right) = \ln 3 + \ln(16) = \ln(3 \times 16) = \ln(48)$$
$$\text{Denominator: } 3\ln 2 + \ln 5 = \ln\left(2^3\right) + \ln 5 = \ln(8) + \ln(5) = \ln(8 \times 5) = \ln(40)$$

Solve for $x$ in the required form $\dfrac{\ln m}{\ln n}$:
$$x = \dfrac{\ln 48}{\ln 40}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Exponential and Logarithmic Equa: Applies the log quotient law, e.g. $\ln(3/5^x)=\ln3-\ln5^x$, or the product law, e.g. $\ln5^x+\ln(2^{3x-4})$; Derives a exact expression for $x$, e.g. $(\ln3+4\ln2)/(3\ln2+\ln5)$; Concludes with $x=\dfrac{\ln48}{\ln40}$.
